title: Verify essential insurance coverage
summary: Health (already addressed), auto, renters or homeowners, and — critically — disability if your employer doesn't provide adequate long-term coverage.
detailsHtml:
Why disability insurance is more important than life insurance for most workers

For a working-age adult, the probability of becoming disabled for 90+ days before retirement is roughly three times the probability of dying. Yet most people carry life insurance (which addresses the lower-probability event) and skip disability insurance (which addresses the higher-probability event). The Social Security Administration's actuarial data confirms this asymmetry.

Coverage benchmark

Aim for long-term disability coverage replacing 60–70% of your income, with a 90- or 180-day elimination period (the longer the elimination period, the lower the premium). Employer-provided coverage often replaces only 40–60% and is taxable on benefits, so a supplemental private policy is frequently warranted.

Term life insurance: Only required if someone depends on your income — spouse, children, aging parents. The amount should be roughly 10–12x annual income for a primary earner with dependents. Whole life and universal life are almost always wrong for accumulation; the fees consume the investment returns the policies advertise. Buy term, invest the difference.

Umbrella liability

Once your net worth exceeds your auto/homeowners liability coverage (typically $300K–$500K), a $1M umbrella policy costs ~$200–$400/year and prevents a single lawsuit from undoing decades of accumulation. Worth purchasing well before you "need" it.
